reference_id: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures
reference_title: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures, 1993 Edition

sections.title: Background
sections.summary: Traces the design procedure lineage from the 1961 AASHO Interim Guide (based on the AASHO Road Test) through the 1972 and 1981 Interim Guides to this 1993 edition, which retains the Road Test performance-prediction equations as the basic model while incorporating flexible-design modifications (resilient-modulus soil support and layer coefficients, environmental factors, reliability, stage construction) and rigid-design modifications (reliability, environmental factors, tied shoulders, subbase erosion, lean subbase design).
sections.body: Following the AASHO Road Test, the AASHO Design Committee developed the 1961 'AASHO Interim Guide for the Design of Rigid and Flexible Pavements,' based on Road Test results supplemented by existing design procedures and (for rigid pavements) available theory. AASHTO published the 'Interim Guide for Design of Pavement Structures--1972,' with 1981 revisions to the rigid pavement design chapter. This 1993 issue retains the AASHO Road Test performance-prediction equations, modified for the 1972 Guide, as the basic design model, with modifications: FLEXIBLE -- (a) soil support number replaced by resilient modulus for a rational, agency-usable material-property test; (b) layer coefficients defined in terms of resilient modulus as well as CBR/R-value; (c) environmental factors (moisture, temperature) objectively included; (d) reliability introduced for risk-based design; (e) stage construction (planned rehabilitation) procedures incorporated. RIGID -- (a) reliability concepts identical to flexible; (b) environmental aspects in the same format as flexible; (c) design procedure modified to include tied shoulders, subbase erosion, and lean subbase design factors. Material is reorganized in a new format: describe the input, present the design equation (nomograph), describe the results.
key_points: Lineage: 1961 AASHO Interim Guide -> 1972 AASHTO Interim Guide -> 1981 rigid-chapter revision -> 1993 edition
Basic design model retained: AASHO Road Test performance-prediction equations
Flexible modifications: resilient-modulus soil support & layer coefficients, environmental factors, reliability, stage construction
Rigid modifications: reliability, environmental factors, tied shoulders/subbase erosion/lean subbase
New format: input -> design equation (nomograph) -> results
sections.applicability: Historical/organizational context for Part II's design procedures.

sections.title: Scope, Limitations, and Organization
sections.summary: Part II provides the detailed design procedure for new construction/reconstruction, assuming the reader has studied Part I first; the procedure is exclusively based on Part II Chapter 2 design requirements and a series of design-equation-solving nomographs, with inherent simplifications relative to the corresponding computer solution. Life-cycle economic analysis (Part I Chapter 3) is strongly recommended alongside the chart procedure.
sections.body: The design procedures of Part II Chapter 3 rely exclusively on the design requirements developed in Part II Chapter 2 plus a series of nomographs solving the design equations. Because of the equations' complexity, computer-based design procedures for both rigid and flexible pavements are treated in separate design manuals; the chart procedures presented here carry inherent assumptions/simplifications that make their solution somewhat less precise than the corresponding computer solution. Both flexible and rigid design approaches permit accounting for both traffic-caused and environmental serviceability loss (Sections 3.1.3/3.2.4 may be skipped if only traffic-caused loss is of interest). A stage-construction option is provided for planned future rehabilitation.
key_points: Part II Chapter 3 design relies exclusively on Chapter 2 design requirements plus solving nomographs
Chart-based nomograph solutions are somewhat less precise than the corresponding computer solution
Both traffic-caused and environmental (swelling/frost heave) serviceability loss can be accounted for
Stage construction option available for planned future rehabilitation
Life-cycle economic analysis (Part I Ch. 3) strongly recommended to compare alternate designs
sections.applicability: Scope/limitations framing before applying the Part II Chapter 2/3 design procedures.
